title: Accessible micro-copy and semantic color tokens for compact cost rows with localized number grouping
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Compact cost rows in the Console (route-level cost tiles, route switcher lists, and density mode cost explorer) currently rely on context-only visual cues and locale-agnostic number formatting. This causes two issues: (1) low-contrast supplementary micro-copy and color cues are not reliably perceivable by users with low vision or under high ambient glare, and (2) number grouping and decimal separators are inconsistent for non-US locales, harming comprehension.

Objective: Design a compact, WCAG-compliant treatment for micro-copy and semantic color tokens that preserves density but improves perceivability, supports keyboard focus affordances, and surfaces locale-correct numeric grouping/formatting. Deliver a prototype and visual spec for engineers to implement tokens, keyboard focus states, and i18n-ready number formatting hooks.

Scope: cost rows in compact density, route inspector baseline, small inline rollouts badges, and the condensed cost-scrubber mini-widget. This ticket covers the design artifacts, acceptance criteria, and prototype testing plan; implementation work will be tracked in the dependent ENG issues.
acceptance_criteria: Compact cost rows use semantic color tokens (success/warn/neutral) with minimum AA contrast ratio 4.5:1 against the background for body text and 3:1 for non-text UI where applicable.
All informational micro-copy beneath numbers is readable at 12px and passes 4.5:1 contrast when rendered on the console background token sets (light and dark themes).
Keyboard focus: each compact row has a visible 3px high-contrast focus ring variant with an accessible offscreen announceable label for screen readers (e.g., 'Route X, cost $Y, details').
Number formatting: prototype demonstrates per-user-locale grouping and decimal separators via CLDR data; examples shown for en-US, de-DE, fr-FR, ja-JP, and hi-IN.
Microcopy: short helper text is concise (<60 characters), provides disambiguation (unit, timeframe), and is localizable via i18n keys with context comments for translators.
Engineering hooks: include token names, focus state classes, and a recommended aria-live/snippet pattern for dynamic cost updates so screen readers are not spammed.
design_workflow_steps: Audit: run a contrast report across existing compact rows and badges (existing results attached).
Sketch: low-fidelity alternatives that preserve density — three variants (token-first, copy-first, hybrid).
Prototype: Figma interactive mini-prototypes for keyboard walkthrough and CLDR-based number toggles.
Usability: quick 5-user a11y pass with VoiceOver and NVDA on prototypes (notes to follow).
Hand-off: deliver tokens table, CSS class names, i18n key suggestions, and acceptance test checklist to ENG.
prototype_notes: Variant A emphasizes semantic tokens with abbreviated micro-copy; Variant B uses subtle separators and expanded micro-copy; Variant C trades a token saturation increase for shorter copy. Keyboard flows documented: Tab to row, Enter expands details, Arrow Up/Down navigate adjacent rows. Prototype includes a toggle for sample locales and screen-reader text toggles to simulate aria-live behavior.
implementation_guidance: Provide CSS tokens: --rw-token-cost-success, --rw-token-cost-warn, --rw-token-cost-neutral. Recommend using Intl.NumberFormat with locale passed from frontend context and fallback to en-US. For focus states use outline-offset: 2px; outline: 3px solid var(--rw-focus-accent). Add aria-label pattern: '{routeName}, cost {localizedNumber}, {helperText}'. Avoid aria-live for every token change; batch updates into a summarized message announced via polite aria-live region on collapse/summary actions.
i18n_instructions: All micro-copy keys should include translator context, unit comments, and pluralization rules where applicable. Example key: console.compactRow.costHelper (context: 'helper text shown under cost, e.g., "per 1K tokens"; do not translate currency symbol'). Include CLDR locale examples in the spec for QA.
qa_test_plan: 1) Contrast checks on light/dark token combos. 2) Keyboard-only navigation pass with focus ring visible on all rows. 3) Screen reader sweep: ensure concise announceable labels and that rapid cost updates are summarized. 4) Locale tests: en-US, de-DE, fr-FR, ja-JP, hi-IN formatting matches spec. 5) Translation verification for expanded languages with no truncation issues.
review_feedback: 2026-03-02 - PM Sasha Liu: please ensure helper copy always includes timeframe (hour/day/month) where ambiguous.
2026-03-05 - Eng lead Marco Rossi: prefer token names to live in runtime theme file; we will map to runtime-1.20 release. Added ENG-80234 as implementation owner.
2026-03-10 - Accessibility consultant: recommended 4.5:1 for small text; suggested adding a high-contrast alternate mode in user settings for power users.
2026-03-12 - Localization lead: add hi-IN number grouping example and note for non-breaking spaces in fr-FR currency formatting.
comments: 2026-03-03 10:12 - Jonah Kim: uploaded initial Figma frames and flagged Variant B as my preferred direction (compact but readable).
2026-03-06 16:33 - Asha Patel: ran a quick pairing with Marco to lock token names; updated spec to call out outline thickness for focus ring.
2026-03-11 09:05 - QA: contrast report attached; found two badge states failing AA on dark theme — marked for follow-up (see attachments).
notes_for_engineers: When implementing Intl.NumberFormat, feature-detect currency formatting capabilities and default to localized units in a single code path. Avoid client-side reflows by precomputing width for compact rows using monospace numerals only when necessary. Provide a toggle data-attribute data-rw-compact='true' for test harness to assert different states.
final_decision: Proceed with Variant B (hybrid): token emphasis with concise helper copy and locale-driven formatting. Include optional high-contrast mode and deliver token table in console-2026.03 release.
